title: Scenario-driven advisor & lightweight guardrails walkthrough for batching + cache
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: design a compact, scenario-driven advisor flow inside the Redwood Console that helps engineers and platform teams pick safe, cost-efficient batching and prefix/KV cache settings. The experience should combine clear recommendations, short explainers about risk/benefit, and non-destructive guardrails (preview, simulation, canary apply + rollback). It needs to be scannable for a fast ops workflow but deep enough for platform engineers to tune policies.
acceptance_criteria: A1: Users can open the Advisor from the model route and select one of 3 workload scenarios (interactive chat, high-throughput embedding, bursty API) and see tailored batching/cache recommendations.
A2: Each recommendation card shows estimated latency delta, token cost delta, and confidence level with an explainability blurb about which prompt patterns are cacheable.
A3: Users can run a simulated preview on a selected time window that shows projected token savings and a list of top N requests that would be affected (anonymized).

A4: Apply flow supports: dry-run preview -> canary (10% traffic) -> full rollout + ability to rollback from the rollout page. Actions are gated by role/permission checks and require an audit log entry.
A5: Design passes accessibility (contrast, keyboard flow) and fits within existing console layout without adding a second navigation level.
A6: Hand-off deliverables include hi-fi Figma frames, interaction spec, copy snippets, and a small token-cost simulator mock component for dev review.
research_notes: Recruitment: 5 participants (2 infra/platform engineers, 2 ML engineers, 1 product engineer).
Key pain: Users conflated prefix caching with request-level caching and were unsure how caching interacts with streaming responses.
Preference: Participants wanted concrete examples ('these 5 prompts will be cached') and an immediate cost preview before applying changes.
Trust: Ops teams preferred gradual application (canary) and visible rollback button; they asked for an audit log entry for compliance.
Edge cases: Streaming chat responses need explicit rules around KV cache prefill and partial tokens; proposed reversible toggles in the UI.
Usability: Compact recommendation cards with one-line rationale + 'why this' explainer had best scan success during tests.
decisions: D1: Use scenario presets (Interactive / Batch embeddings / Burst API) as primary entry to reduce cognitive load for new users.
D2: Surface three key metrics on cards only: latency impact, token cost delta, and recommendation confidence. Deep details available on expand.
D3: Simulated preview will operate on sampled historical traffic (anonymized) provided by backend -> UI will show top-10 example requests affected.
D4: Apply pipeline = dry-run preview -> canary (10% by default) with automatic monitoring -> full rollout. Rollback action must be one-click and produce an audit log event.
D5: Guardrails: default conservative prefix detection, opt-in aggressive prescreening; require user to acknowledge risk for aggressive caching.
D6: Accessibility: follow existing Console motion patterns; ensure keyboard-first interactions and screen-reader labels for recommendation cards.
D7: Copy: use plain-language explainers (avoid jargon) with short FAQ link to docs for advanced operators.
D8: Implementation split: UI will be stateless client for previews; backend endpoints ENG-6220 and ENG-6287 will provide simulation and apply APIs.
